After the [fall of the Soviet Union](/wiki/Fall_of_the_Soviet_Union "Fall of the Soviet Union") in 1991, historical records were released to allow the true accounting of Soviet lunar efforts. Unlike the U.S. tradition of assigning a particular mission name in advance of a launch, the Soviets assigned a public "[Luna](/wiki/Luna_programme "Luna programme")" mission number only if a launch resulted in a spacecraft going beyond Earth orbit. The policy had the effect of hiding Soviet Moon mission failures from public view.

If the attempt failed in Earth orbit before departing for the Moon, it was frequently, but not always, given a "[Sputnik](/wiki/Sputnik_programme "Sputnik programme")" or "[Cosmos](/wiki/Cosmos_(satellite) "Cosmos (satellite)")" Earth-orbit mission number to hide its purpose. Launch explosions were not acknowledged at all.

The war ended on 9 May 1945, when Germany's armed forces [surrendered unconditionally](/wiki/Unconditional_surrender "Unconditional surrender") following the [Battle of Berlin](/wiki/Battle_of_Berlin "Battle of Berlin") (also known as the [Berlin Offensive](/wiki/Berlin_Offensive "Berlin Offensive")), a strategic operation executed by the Red Army.

The states that provided forces and other resources for the German war effort included the Axis Powers – primarily Romania, Hungary, Italy, pro-Nazi Slovakia, and Croatia. The [Acts of Union 1707](/wiki/Acts_of_Union_1707 "Acts of Union 1707") declared that the [Kingdom of England](/wiki/Kingdom_of_England "Kingdom of England") and the [Kingdom of Scotland](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Scotland "Kingdom of Scotland") were "United into One Kingdom by the Name of Great Britain".[[p]](#cite_note-34)[[19]](#cite_note-Acts_of_Union_1707-35) The term "United Kingdom" has occasionally been used for the former [Kingdom of Great Britain](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain"), although its official name from 1707 to 1800 was simply "Great Britain".[[20]](#cite_note-36) The [Acts of Union 1800](/wiki/Acts_of_Union_1800 "Acts of Union 1800") formed the [United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland](/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"). Following the [partition of Ireland](/wiki/Partition_of_Ireland "Partition of Ireland") and the independence of the [Irish Free State](/wiki/Irish_Free_State "Irish Free State") in 1922, which left [Northern Ireland](/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland") as the only part of the island of Ireland within the United Kingdom, the name was changed in 1927 to the "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland".[[21]](#cite_note-37)

**Darrell Clayton Hammond** (born October 8, 1955)[[1]](#cite_note-tvg-1) is an American actor, comedian, impressionist, and announcer. He was a regular cast member on the [NBC](/wiki/NBC "NBC") [sketch comedy](/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") series *[Saturday Night Live](/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")* from 1995 to 2009, and has been its announcer since 2014.

Upon his departure from the cast in 2009, Hammond, at age 53, was the oldest cast member in the show's history. He has made more *SNL* appearances than any other cast member besides [Kenan Thompson](/wiki/Kenan_Thompson "Kenan Thompson"), and impersonated more than 107 celebrities, with [Bill Clinton](/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") as his most frequent impression.[[2]](#cite_note-2) On September 19, 2014, Hammond was announced as the new announcer of *SNL,* replacing [Don Pardo](/wiki/Don_Pardo "Don Pardo"), who had died the month before.[[3]](#cite_note-NYT-3)
